title: Tactical Egress Guard: Terraform module for outbound policy, SGs, NACLs, and private DNS
creator: Leah Park
description:
Goal: Build a composable Terraform module that standardizes outbound/egress controls for Private (VPC) deployments. The module will manage security groups (SGs), network ACLs (NACLs) for subnet-level hardening, optional Private DNS forwarding rules for internal service resolution, and a policy-layer for allowed egress destinations (CIDR and FQDN). It must be consumable by both Redwood Private and Dedicated stacks with clear upgrade paths and CI-gated validations.

Scope and responsibilities:
- Provide opinionated defaults aligned with Redwood security guidelines (deny-by-default, explicit allow lists for control plane and telemetry).
- Expose overridable inputs for customers to add allow rules, trusted proxies, and service endpoints.
- Implement a policy config object (policy-as-data) that compiles into SG/NACL entries and optional egress firewall rules.
- Integrate Private DNS: optional Route 53 Resolver inbound/outbound rules + conditional private hosted zone attachments.
- Add pre-apply checks: plan-time linting (tflint/custom checks), Terraform validate, and a policy simulator that can detect rules that accidentally open broad egress (e.g., 0.0.0.0/0 on high-priority ports).
- Provide automated health checks that run post-apply: synthetic egress tests from a bastion/runner to validate blocking/allowing behavior, DNS resolution tests, and a drift detection job (periodic compare of actual security group rules vs module intent).

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- SG vs NACL: SGs are stateful and easier for instance-level rules; NACLs provide subnet-level enforcement. We'll generate both when a strict deployment mode is enabled. Default will be SG-first to preserve simplicity; strict mode creates mirrored NACL entries.
- Policy-as-data: store canonical policy in module inputs as list of rules (name, description, ports, cidr/fqdn, env scope). This enables generating Terraform resources deterministically and powering the simulator. Downside: slightly more verbose input for customers; upside: easier testing and drift detection.
- Private DNS integration will be opt-in to avoid accidental cross-account host resolution. When enabled, the module wires resolver endpoints and outputs a binding manifest for higher-level stacks to attach.

Upgrade & migration strategy:
1) Introduce module v0.1 with opt-in features behind flags (strict_nacl = false, private_dns = false).
2) Provide a migration script (python/Go) that computes plan diffs for existing SG rules and suggests a minimal set of Terraform resources to import into state. Store suggested terraform import commands in the module docs and as CI job output.
3) For breaking changes (resolving rule naming, resource renames), follow semver and a deprecation cycle: mark deprecated inputs and maintain compatibility for one minor release with generated warnings in plan.
4) Promote a canary rollout pattern: create a non-prod workspace that applies the module with a narrow allow-list, run the synthetic health checks, and only then promote to prod workspaces.

Testing & CI:
- Unit: Terratest suite to validate that given policy-as-data inputs the module emits expected SG/NACL resources.
- Integration: GitHub Actions that create ephemeral VPC + minimal compute to run e2e checks (egress allow/block, DNS resolution). Tests run in non-prod regions only.
- Policy lint: custom policy rules executed as part of pre-apply (scripts in tools/egress-assert).
- PR gating: terraform plan must be clean, tests must pass, and a human reviewer from Security must approve for security_review_required = true.

Observability & health checks:
- Create a 'TacticalEgress/health' dashboard in Console showing last synthetic test results, drift count, and recent security rule changes (audit logs).
- Export actionable CloudWatch/Stackdriver metrics: egress_allowed_count, egress_blocked_count, dns_resolution_failures.
- Implement an on-demand validation endpoint (internal API) that runs a targeted test from a specified subnet and returns pass/fail and logs.

Docs & rollout artifacts:
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Tactical+Egress+Guard+Design (draft)
- Example consumption: examples/private/with-redis-and-proxy.tf in repo (WIP)
- Migration helper: tools/egress_migrate.py (generates import commands)

Acceptance criteria:
- Module published to registry with v0.1 and sample usage for Private and Dedicated stacks.
- Terratest and integration tests pass in CI.
- Health check runner established and traffic-sim tests validate allow/deny decisions.
- Security sign-off obtained and runbooks updated.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: accidental production outage when tightening rules. Mitigation: default to opt-in strict mode and require canary workspace validation plus automatic rollback on failed health checks.
- Risk: Terraform state import complexity. Mitigation: provide a migration helper and run an import dry-run in CI to detect surprises.

Next steps:
- Week 1 (this cycle): scaffold module inputs/resources, basic SG creation, Terratest skeleton.
- Week 2: implement policy-as-data compiler, pre-apply lint, and initial integration tests.
- Week 3: private DNS wiring and health-check runner; security review.
